lines.text: Can a 200 dollar hydrogen kit really cut your fuel use by 35 percent?
He bolts it to a Suburban so it splits water into gas and feeds it into the engine.
But splitting water takes more energy than burning that gas gives back so the math was never going to work.
beats: ai:a water molecule splitting into glowing hydrogen and oxygen atoms on a bright white lab background

lines.text: On the 0 to 60 runs the truck is slower with hydrogen three out of four times.
So the extra power claim falls flat right away.
Next he tests it on a fuel injected generator with half a liter of gas.
Without hydrogen it runs 19 minutes and 46 seconds.
And with hydrogen it dies nine seconds sooner so the kit made it slightly worse.
Then he doubles the electrolyte to make twice the gas and it runs 21 seconds shorter.
Because the generator has to make the power for the kit so the engine just burns extra fuel to feed it.
beats: ai:bright blue electric current flowing from a yellow generator into a small black box in a sunlit workshop
ai:close up of a small engine exhaust puffing in a bright sunny workshop with a fuel gauge dropping

lines.text: And after 250 miles the spark plug looks exactly the same so it didn't even clean the engine.
So would you put 200 dollars of hydrogen on your car?
